title: Hospital-physician collaboration: landscape of economic integration and impact on clinical integration

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Hospital-physician collaboration: landscape of economic integration and impact on clinical integration》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Findings · abstract-3-1】The goals of the two parties in HPRs overlap only partly, and their primary aim is not reducing cost or improving quality. The evidence base for the impact of many models of economic integration is either weak or nonexistent, with only a few models of economic integration having robust effects. The relationship between economic and clinical integration also is weak and inconsistent. There are several possible reasons for this weak linkage and many barriers to further integration between hospitals and physicians.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Hospital-physician collaboration: landscape of economic integration and impact on clinical integration》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】This article analyzes the HPRs that focus on the economic integration of hospitals and physicians and the goals that HPRs are designed to achieve. It then reviews the literature on the impact of HPRs on cost, quality, and clinical integration.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Hospital-physician collaboration: landscape of economic integration and impact on clinical integration》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Findings · abstract-3-1】The goals of the two parties in HPRs overlap only partly, and their primary aim is not reducing cost or improving quality. The evidence base for the impact of many models of economic integration is either weak or nonexistent, with only a few models of economic integration having robust effects. The relationship between economic and clinical integration also is weak and inconsistent. There are several possible reasons for this weak linkage and many barriers to further integration between hospitals and physicians.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】Successful HPRs may require better financial conditions for physicians, internal changes to clinical operations, application of behavioral skills to the management of HPRs, changes in how providers are paid, and systemic changes encompassing several types of integration simultaneously.
